title: Windows 11 - Failled to built whisper.cpp for Nvidia cublas
body: I'm on Windows 11. I installed and updated Visual Studio 2022, installed CUDA 12.2.0 and later 12.2.2, and installed CMake 3.27.4. When I run `cmake . --fresh -DWHISPER_CUBLAS=ON`, CMake finds CUDA 12.2 and cuBLAS but fails while compiling `CMakeCUDACompilerId.cu`. MSBuild reports `MSB3686: Unable to create Xaml task` and says a generated `.cs` file under `C:\windows\TEMP` could not be found.

symptoms_visible: When I configure whisper.cpp with `WHISPER_CUBLAS=ON`, CMake finds CUDA 12.2 and cuBLAS but stops while identifying the CUDA compiler.
MSBuild reports `MSB3686: Unable to create Xaml task` and says a generated source file under `C:\windows\TEMP` could not be found.
N0.label: N0 CUDA compiler identification failure reported

symptoms_visible: When I explicitly pass the CUDA 12.2 `nvcc.exe` path as `CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER`, configuration still ends with the same CUDA compiler-identification and MSB3686 errors.
N1.label: N1 explicit nvcc probe completed

symptoms_visible: With both `CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER` and `CUDATOOLKITDIR` pointed at CUDA 12.2, CMake still finds cuBLAS and then stops with the same MSB3686 Xaml-task and missing temporary source-file errors.
N2.label: N2 CUDA toolkit directory probe completed

symptoms_visible: I have tried the suggestions so far, but I still cannot configure and build the CUDA-enabled version.
N3.label: N3 build remains blocked after configuration probes

symptoms_visible: After reinstalling Windows 11 with the option to keep my applications and user files, I can configure and compile the CUDA-enabled version successfully from a fresh build directory.
N_terminal.label: terminal CUDA build succeeds after Windows environment repair

question_patterns: Could you rerun CMake while explicitly setting `CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER` to the full path of `nvcc.exe` and paste the result?
Does pointing CMake directly at your CUDA compiler change the compiler-identification error?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried both an in-tree configure and a separate build directory with `CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER` set to `C:\Program Files\NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit\CUDA\v12.2\bin\nvcc.exe`. I get the same errors as in my first post.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With the full `nvcc.exe` path, CMake identifies the CUDA compiler and the build completes.
I used the same CUDA 12.2 compiler path from a separate build directory and received the identical MSB3686 output.

edges.comment: Issue c0-c1, reporter's Windows 11 system: participant1 requested the explicit compiler-path probe, and the reporter supplied the commands and raw result. This is a handler-initiated configuration measurement, not a persistent fix.

question_patterns: Could you point `CUDATOOLKITDIR` at the installed CUDA directory and rerun the configure command?
What output do you get when both the CUDA compiler and toolkit directory are specified explicitly?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran CMake with `CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER` set to the CUDA 12.2 `nvcc.exe` and `CUDATOOLKITDIR` set to `C:\Program Files\NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit\CUDA\v12.2`. It still finds CUDA and cuBLAS, then produces the same MSB3686 Xaml-task and missing temporary `.cs` file errors.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After setting the toolkit directory, CMake identifies CUDA and the release build succeeds.
The toolkit is reported as version 12.2.91 rather than just 12.2, but the same MSBuild error follows.

edges.comment: Issue c2-c3, reporter's system: participant1 proposed setting the toolkit directory; the reporter ran the corresponding CMake probe and pasted the unchanged raw build output.

question_patterns: After trying the suggestions so far, what is the current observable build result?
Are you still seeing the original compiler-identification error?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried everything suggested and still cannot build it. I am getting the same errors and was about ready to give up.

edges.comment: Issue c4-c9, reporter's system: after further discussion and the suggestion to reinstall CUDA and Visual Studio, the reporter stated only that they had tried everything and remained unable to build. The graph does not invent a specifically confirmed reinstall attempt.

solution.intent: Treat the MSBuild Xaml-task and missing temporary source-file failure as damage in the Windows system environment rather than CUDA discovery: clean or repair the Windows system-variable paths, using an in-place Windows repair installation if necessary, then configure in a fresh build directory and verify a release build with cuBLAS enabled.
solution.concrete_example: Inspect the Windows system environment and remove corrupt or unnecessary PATH entries. In the reporter's case, reinstalling Windows 11 with 'keep installed applications and user files' repaired the environment. They then used VS 2022, CUDA Toolkit 11.6.1 and CMake, followed by `mkdir build`, `cmake.exe -B build -D WHISPER_CUBLAS=1`, and `cmake.exe --build build --config release`, which completed successfully.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the MSBuild error and the unchanged results from explicit CUDA compiler/toolkit probes. Recognizing that an MSB3686 Xaml-task failure with a missing generated file under the Windows TEMP directory points beyond whisper.cpp's CUDA discovery and toward a damaged Windows environment is engineer-side inference. The reporter later independently attributed the resolved problem to corrupted Windows system-variable paths.

edges.comment: Issue c10-c12, reporter's system: participant2 connected this error class with an unhealthy or excessively long PATH. The reporter then repaired Windows 11 while retaining applications and files and personally confirmed a successful clean CUDA build. Comments c13-c15 concern later participants and different CUDA installations, so they are not spliced into the opening reporter's causal chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as corrupted or unhealthy Windows system environment-variable paths causing the MSBuild Xaml-task and temporary-file failure, rather than a whisper.cpp source error or failure to locate cuBLAS.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: CMake already finds CUDA and cuBLAS, while explicitly setting `CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER` and `CUDATOOLKITDIR` leaves the same MSB3686 error.
Must not present either explicit CUDA compiler selection or setting the toolkit directory as the resolution; both were tested on the reporter's system with the same observable failure.

The resolution must repair or clean the Windows environment, with the reporter's in-place Windows 11 repair installation as the known successful method, and then use a fresh out-of-source CMake configure and release build.
Must ask the reporter to verify that the CUDA-enabled build completes successfully after the environment repair before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical Windows user who can install Visual Studio, CUDA and CMake, run PowerShell commands, and paste detailed build logs, but needs guidance on compiler and environment configuration.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent and direct, with short follow-ups and full command output; becomes visibly frustrated after repeated failures but clearly documents the eventual successful procedure.
